802 Calculating the Length of a Shorter Side

examples.solution_text:
First find the shared side.
$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{8^{2}+6^{2}}\\y&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
This is a shorter side of the second right-angled triangle.
$\begin{align*}x&=\sqrt{10^{2}+y^{2}}\\x&=\sqrt{10^{2}+10^{2}}\\x&=\sqrt{200}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Find the shared hypotenuse first.
$\begin{align*}x&=\sqrt{6^{2}+8^{2}}\\x&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
The second triangle has hypotenuse $15\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{15^{2}-x^{2}}\\y&=\sqrt{225-100}\\y&=\sqrt{125}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The two end sections of the base are equal.
$\begin{align*}x&=(18-10)\div2\\x&=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Use the height and one end section to find a sloping side.
$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{4^{2}+7^{2}}\\y&=\sqrt{65}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Keep the sloping length exact until the final calculation.
$\begin{align*}P&=18+10+2\sqrt{65}\\P&\approx44.1\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The horizontal leg of the right-angled triangle is $24-19=5\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{align*}s&=\sqrt{5^{2}+12^{2}}\\s&=13\text{ cm}\\P&=24+19+12+13\\P&=68.0\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Both halves of the vertical diagonal are $7\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Left side}&=\sqrt{12^{2}+7^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{193}\text{ cm}\\\text{Right side}&=\sqrt{9^{2}+7^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{130}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Add both pairs of sides, keeping their lengths exact.
$\begin{align*}P&=2\sqrt{193}+2\sqrt{130}\\P&\approx50.6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The perpendicular from the centre bisects the water surface, so half its width is $15\text{ cm}$. Let $h$ be the distance from the centre to the surface.
$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{17^{2}-15^{2}}\\h&=\sqrt{64}\\h&=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Subtract this distance from the radius.
$\begin{align*}d&=17-8\\d&=9\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The perpendicular from the tower bisects the road segment within range. Let $h$ be half this segment.
$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{25^{2}-9^{2}}\\h&=\sqrt{544}\text{ km}\end{align*}$
Double the exact intermediate length, then round.
$\begin{align*}x&=2\sqrt{544}\\x&\approx46.65\text{ km}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: y² = 8² + 6² = 100, so y = 10 cm. Then x² = 10² + 100 = 200, so x = √200 cm.
x² = 6² + 8² = 100, so x = 10 cm. Then y² = 15² − 100 = 125, so y = √125 cm. The authored vectors at the shared vertex are perpendicular.
Each base extension is (18 − 10)/2 = 4 cm. Each sloping side is √(4² + 7²) = √65 cm. P = 28 + 2√65 = 44.1245… cm, giving 44.1 cm.
The horizontal leg is 24 − 19 = 5 cm. The sloping side is √(5² + 12²) = 13 cm. P = 24 + 19 + 12 + 13 = 68.0 cm.
The two side lengths are √(12² + 7²) = √193 cm and √(9² + 7²) = √130 cm. P = 2√193 + 2√130 = 50.5884… cm, giving 50.6 cm.

Half the surface width is 15 cm. The centre-to-surface distance is √(17² − 15²) = 8 cm. Since the surface lies below the centre, d = 17 − 8 = 9 cm. The diagram's radius and chord coordinates agree with these lengths.
Half the covered road length is √(25² − 9²) = √544 km. The total is 2√544 = 46.6476… km, giving 46.65 km. The drawn chord endpoints agree with the radius and perpendicular distance.
